blocks.text: Docker's success created pressure for vendor-neutral standards, so the image format and runtime were standardized in the OCI (2015) and Docker's engine was split into reusable components: runc for running containers, containerd for managing them.

rows: Image spec, runtime spec, later distribution spec
Runtimes plug in via an interface (containerd, CRI-O)
Kubernetes stops using Docker Engine directly; images unaffected

blocks.src: generate: Before/after: a monolithic Docker daemon on the left; on the right, docker CLI → dockerd → containerd → shim → runc, with Kubernetes kubelet → CRI → containerd/CRI-O alongside
blocks.caption: Docker's split into standard components.

items: No lock-in: build with Docker, BuildKit, Buildah or kaniko; run with containerd, CRI-O or Podman.
"Kubernetes deprecated Docker" meant the runtime shim, not Docker-built images.
Alternative runtimes (gVisor, Kata) plug in under the same specs.

blocks.text: Q: "Kubernetes removed dockershim. Do Docker images still work?" A: "Yes. Images built with Docker are OCI images, and Kubernetes runs them through containerd or CRI-O via the CRI. Only the Docker Engine integration was removed."

items: Docker split into dockerd → containerd → runc.
Kubernetes uses containerd/CRI-O, not Docker Engine.
